transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-08-04 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (CTO, Kestrel), Sofia Martinez (Platform Eng), Tom Howard (ML Infra), Lena (Data Science), Jae (Security)

Summary:
Kestrel AI is evaluating an exit from their current OpenAI/Azure-hosted stack and replatforming parts of their inference to Redwood. Primary drivers: cost control for high-volume token workloads, deterministic latency for streaming chat, and desire to use vLLM/TGI-based runtime for advanced caching and quantization. Security wants SOC2 + KMS support. Technical team wants parity with current model outputs (eval parity) and compatibility with TGI/vLLM config flags. The call covered architecture options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), compatibility gaps, proposed benchmark plan, and next steps.

Topics covered:
- Migration drivers: cost, latency, vendor lock-in
- Model/runtime compatibility: vLLM, TGI, tokenizer differences
- Eval parity approach: test harness, metrics, thresholds
- Hosting options: Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, RBAC, audit logs
- Performance knobs: batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization, kernel choices
- Pricing/profile ask: Dedicated with burst, pricing model impact of caching

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey all, thanks for taking time — quick roll call?
[00:05] Rajiv Menon: Rajiv here, CTO, hi.
[00:07] Sofia Martinez: Sofia.
[00:09] Tom Howard: Tom.
[00:12] Lena: Lena.
[00:13] Jae: Jae, security.
[00:16] Diego Alvarez: Diego from Redwood, SE.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Great. Quick agenda: understand what you're running today, constraints, what parity means for you, and then propose an evaluation path. Sound good?
[00:25] Rajiv Menon: Yep. To summarize, we run a hybrid. We use OpenAI for a lot of multi-tenant customer-facing chat and Anthropic for some safety-sensitive paths. On-prem we've been experimenting with vLLM and TGI for batching and caching because cost's ballooned. We're trying to figure out if we move everything to Redwood Hosted or go Dedicated or Private. Biggest asks are: 1) output parity with current API responses (we track similarity and some business metrics), 2) predictable P95 for streaming, 3) SOC2+KMS.
[01:00] Diego Alvarez: Makes sense. A few clarifying q's: what models are you using and do you have custom finetunes or embeddings that need migration?
[01:07] Rajiv Menon: Mostly GPT-4-ish style via OpenAI, but we've also got a fine-tuned 7B on TGI for summarization. Embeddings are mixed — OpenAI embeddings and a local SBERT variant. We do store customer vectors in-house.
[01:20] Sofia Martinez: And infra wise, latency SLO is 300ms P95 for short-turn chat, and for long-form summarization we care more about cost and throughput.
[01:30] Tom Howard: For vLLM we use a combination of KV cache tricks and custom tokenizers. Concern is whether Redwood's runtime will honor the same kv prefetch semantics and TGI flags (like --no-cuda-... ooops) sorry, tmi.
[01:44] Diego Alvarez: No that's good — runtime semantics matter. Short answer: Redwood runtime supports KV caching and prefix caching patterns and we can accept TGI/vLLM model artifacts in many cases, but there are caveats around tokenizer mismatch and certain model-ops that expect custom kernel ops. We'll need your model artifacts and the exact TGI/vLLM config to confirm.
[02:10] Rajiv Menon: When you say "accept" — does that mean we can drop in the exact TGI artifact we built on our side? We don't want to retrain or reexport if possible.
[02:18] Diego Alvarez: Often yes; we've onboarded many TGI builds. There are two typical compatibility classes: 1) plain HF-flavored ggml/pt checkpoints that map cleanly, and 2) heavily patched TGI artifacts or custom CUDA kernels — those may require minor conversion or fallback to a comparable variant. We try to keep same tokenizer and same sampling seeds to help parity.
[02:37] Lena: Speaking of parity, our data team measures BLEU-ish and a business metric of "helpful answer rate" across prompts. What's your suggested eval harness?
[02:46] Maya Chen: We usually do side-by-side runs: you supply a representative prompt set (200-500 prompts of different lengths), we run them against your current provider and our candidate model/runtime combos, and compute: semantic similarity, discrete diff count, and business metric lift. We'll also capture latency distributions and cost per 1M tokens.
[03:08] Rajiv Menon: How do you handle sampling/pseudorandomness? Our customers can observe small output diffs.
[03:13] Diego Alvarez: We run deterministic sampling where feasible (fixed temperature/seed) and also compare stochastic outputs with a similarity threshold. We also have tooling to align tokenization (normalize whitespace, bert-vs-gpt token fuzz). Small diffs are expected but we sign off on thresholds.
[03:28] Jae: Security: SOC2 is a must. Also, KMS for keys and customer data encryption at rest, audit logs, SSO with our Okta, and RBAC.
[03:39] Maya Chen: Redwood Hosted is SOC2 and supports KMS integrations + SSO/RBAC. For Private we provide a customer-managed control plane and on-prem options with HSM/KMS integrations as well. We'll send the SOC2 summary after the call.
[03:52] Sofia Martinez: Ok, good. A chunk of our workload is bursty — black friday-like events — and we need burst capacity. How does Dedicated burst work?
[04:00] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools; you can enable burst with autoscale into shared pools. There's a delta price for burst. On Dedicated we can tune batching window and conservative latency targets; on Hosted you get elastic capacity but less isolation. We can run numbers once we have your token profile.
[04:18] Tom Howard: Token profile — our average chat is 80 tokens input, 160 output. Summarization jobs are 2k tokens.
[04:25] Maya Chen: That's helpful. For 2k sequences we recommend a specific kernel selection and quantization path — we'd propose int8 with an eval to verify quality.
[04:33] Rajiv Menon: Quantization — we saw big cost wins but worried about quality regression for summarization.
[04:39] Diego Alvarez: Totally. Redwood Optimize provides recommendations and we can run A/B quality checks with regen tests to ensure no regression. We'll flag model-level quant profiles per workload.
[04:50] Lena: Any gotchas about moving embeddings? We use OpenAI embeddings for search scoring.
[04:55] Diego Alvarez: Two paths: 1) keep using OpenAI embeddings while moving generation to Redwood, 2) move embeddings to an in-house or open model on Redwood. Option 1 is fastest; option 2 reduces external spend but needs an evaluation for semantic parity.
[05:10] Rajiv Menon: Our procurement/legal asks about data residency — some EU customers need EU region hosting. Does Redwood support regional pinning?
[05:17] Maya Chen: Yes — regional routing and model hosting in specific cloud regions is supported. For Private you can host entirely in your VPC/region.
[05:24] Jae: About audit logs — retention and export formats?
[05:27] Diego Alvarez: We can set retention policies and export to your SIEM in common formats. We'll include details in the security pack.
[05:34] Rajiv Menon: Performance question: you mentioned prefix caching earlier. We're using aggressive prefix caching in vLLM to reduce tokens. Will Redwood's cache be compatible?
[05:42] Diego Alvarez: Redwood runtime supports prefix and KV caching. Two notes: 1) cache hits depend on exact tokenization and prompt normalization, so we might need to canonicalize prompts. 2) we support shared cache across sessions depending on routing and model variant. That can massively reduce tokens for multi-turn chat.
[06:00] Sofia Martinez: If caching reduces tokens, that affects billing. How do you bill cached tokens?
[06:04] Maya Chen: We bill based on compute and emitted tokens; caching reduces compute and overall token counts. For Dedicated we can show modeled cost impact in the proposal.
[06:13] Tom Howard: Can we do a private deployment but keep Redwood console connectivity for observability?
[06:18] Diego Alvarez: Yes — hybrid control plane: customer-managed data plane with optional reporting to the Redwood console under a VPC peering or secure export. Logs can be exported to your splunk/ELK.
[06:30] Rajiv Menon: Any customers who moved from OpenAI+TGI locally to Redwood? Curious about real output hits.
[06:36] Diego Alvarez: We have examples; some customers kept exact model artifacts and achieved >95% similarity on business metrics after minor tokenizer alignment. A few had to accept small regen thresholds. We'll share anonymized case studies.
[06:50] Lena: Special question: we have a custom sampling wrapper that overrides top_p and nucleus at runtime — do we need to modify that for Redwood?
[06:58] Diego Alvarez: Our runtime supports dynamic sampling parameters. If it's purely a wrapper, we can map it. Edge cases are custom CUDA ops invoked in sampling; those would need a check.
[07:10] Maya Chen: Let's talk timeline — what's your desired go-live?
[07:13] Rajiv Menon: We'd like a pilot in Q4, ideally a production cutover by Q1 if benchmarks look good.
[07:20] Maya Chen: Sounds reasonable. Proposal: 1) drop us 200-500 prompts+dataset slice and current config 2) Redwood SE runs a benchmark and parity check 3) joint review and then a 2-week pilot on Dedicated or Private.
[07:34] Rajiv Menon: Cost sensitivity is high. We'll want clear metrics before we sign.
[07:39] Maya Chen: Agreed. We'll provide a cost model and a sensitivity analysis showing savings from caching + quantization.
[07:47] Tom Howard: One last technical: our TGI exports use custom attention kernel forks — would that require us to rebuild?
[07:54] Diego Alvarez: If it's a custom kernel, we have options: run the model in a compatibility mode with lower perf, or work with our runtime team to incorporate the kernel (which can add time). We'll evaluate after we see the artifact.
[08:09] Sofia Martinez: Ok thanks.
[08:11] Maya Chen: Quick recap of next steps — I'll send SOC2 doc + deployment checklist; Diego will take your TGI artifact and run a smoke parity; Rajiv will share prompts and token profile. We'll schedule the benchmark week of 8/17. Anything else?
[08:26] Rajiv Menon: Pricing for Dedicated with burst, and a first-cut estimate of cost savings for prefix caching.
[08:31] Maya Chen: We'll include that in the follow-up email.
[08:34] Jae: Also, include SSO and KMS integration steps.
[08:37] Maya Chen: Yep. Thanks everyone.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had a few misattributions (sometimes "Diego" typed as "Dego"), a couple truncated sentences, some code flags were spoken quickly (TGI args). We retained filler and interruptions to keep authenticity.

End of call recap:
- Decision criteria: eval parity, P95 latency, SOC2/KMS compliance, cost delta
- Proposed evaluation: sample prompts -> SE parity runs -> joint review -> pilot on Dedicated/Private

References mentioned: Redwood security pack (link to be sent), benchmark template (link to be sent), anonymized case study on TGI migrations (will be shared)
